walkthroughs.body_html:
Nucleic Acids — a core area of Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nucleic Acids brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nucleic Acids.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.
From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
